content: Replace the repository's narrower expert-skill form with the official Codex skill package contract, preserve existing durable skill links, provide native Codex discovery, and add an evidence-backed implementation-readiness expert skill.

Researched the official OpenAI Codex Build skills documentation and primary readiness sources from SEI ATAM, Google SRE reliable launches, NASA technology readiness levels, and Thoughtworks evolutionary architecture and fitness functions.

The OpenAI Codex package contract is authoritative: uppercase SKILL.md with name and description is the minimum; agents/openai.yaml, scripts, references, and assets are optional. Repository lifecycle status moved out of SKILL.md frontmatter into the existing catalog index. Physical packages remain under agent/skills for historical links, while .agents/skills is a checked symlink for native Codex discovery.

Implementation readiness is reported as four independent lanes: architecture baseline, workstream activation, implementation maturity, and release/operations readiness. Lanes are never averaged; open decisions are classified by latest safe closure point, and important quality attributes require executable fitness evidence.

All five repository skills passed the bundled skill-creator quick_validate.py. The stdlib repository validator passed, and its synthetic suite expanded from 23 to 29 cases covering minimal and extended Codex frontmatter, optional package resources, name/path agreement, legacy status rejection, and discovery-symlink drift.

The dev preset configured and built cleanly; ctest --preset dev --output-on-failure passed 16/16 tests, including metaflux.architecture.agent-records-selftest and metaflux.architecture.component-graph.

The isolated Nix agent-records and entry-points derivations passed with the .agents/skills symlink preserved in the source snapshot. nix flake check path:. -L ended with all checks passed after transient binary-cache network retries.

Content commit 12efb20e52e215fdfc70a3d4a59c2fc46bfcf4d9 records the Codex package migration, native discovery entry point, implementation-readiness skill and references, validator rules and tests, and Nix source/check coverage. No product constraint, architecture decision, or open-decision ledger row changed.
